html:
The Blackfoot, who call themselves Niitsitapi, "the original people", are an Algonquian-speaking confederacy of the northwestern Great Plains, in today's Alberta and Montana. The confederacy joins the Siksika, the Kainai (Blood) and the Piikani (Peigan).

On foot, they hunted bison by driving herds over cliffs, as at Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump. After horses and guns reached them in the 1700s they became one of the strongest powers on the northern Plains, ranging from the North Saskatchewan River to the Yellowstone. Smallpox in 1781 and 1837 hit them hard.

In 1870 the US Army killed about 200 Piikani, mostly women, children and old people, in the Marias Massacre. In 1877 the Canadian bands signed Treaty 7. The destruction of the bison by the early 1880s brought famine. See also Blackfoot.
